content: Chlorthalidone, commonly referred to as a water pill, is prescribed to manage high blood pressure and fluid retention caused by various conditions, including heart disease. It works by prompting the kidneys to eliminate excess water and salt from the body through urine. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Chlorthalidone is available in tablet form and is typically taken orally once daily or every other day, preferably after a meal such as breakfast. It is recommended to take this medication in the morning to minimize nighttime urination. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take chlorthalidone exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed. While chlorthalidone helps control high blood pressure, it does not cure it. Continue taking it even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. Chlorthalidone may also be used to treat conditions such as diabetes insipidus, certain electrolyte imbalances, and to prevent kidney stones in patients with elevated calcium levels in their blood. Discuss the potential risks of using this medication for your specific condition with your doctor. Before taking chlorthalidone, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to chlorthalidone, sulfa drugs, or any other medications. Provide a list of all medications you are taking, including prescription and non-prescription drugs, vitamins, and supplements. If you are taking cholestyramine or colestipol, take them at least one hour after chlorthalidone. Notify your doctor if you have a history of diabetes, gout, or kidney, liver, thyroid, or parathyroid disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking chlorthalidone, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your healthcare provider that you are taking chlorthalidone. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how it affects you. Alcohol can exacerbate drowsiness caused by this drug. Additionally, avoid unnecessary or prolonged sun exposure, and use protective clothing, sunglasses, and sunscreen, as chlorthalidone may increase your skin's sensitivity to sunlight. Follow your doctor’s dietary instructions while taking chlorthalidone. Your doctor may recommend consuming potassium-rich foods, such as bananas, prunes, raisins, and orange juice, to maintain proper potassium levels. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Frequent urination is a common side effect that typically subsides after a few weeks of use. Notify your doctor if you experience severe or persistent symptoms such as muscle weakness, dizziness, cramps, excessive thirst, stomach pain, upset stomach, vomiting, diarrhea, loss of appetite, headache, or hair loss. If you experience serious side effects such as a sore throat with fever, unusual bleeding or bruising, severe skin rash with peeling, or difficulty breathing or swallowing, contact your doctor immediately. Serious side effects can be reported to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store chlorthalidone in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of expired or unneeded medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance on disposal. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call 911 immediately. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory for regular monitoring of your blood pressure and occasional blood tests. Do not share your medication with others. Consult your pharmacist if you have questions about refilling your prescription.
